text.card: Complete a three-by-three digit square using row, column and ordering clues.
text.hands_empty: Put down what you hold before changing an indicator.
text.occupied: Clear that cell before placing a different digit.
text.repeated: That digit already appears in this row or column. Clear a conflicting choice.
text.order: These two filled cells would violate the fixed strict inequality. Clear or choose another digit.
text.already_blank: That cell is already blank. Choose a filled mutable cell to clear.
text.coordinates: Rows1 to3 run from the far/top edge toward the near/bottom edge; columns1 to3 run left to right. Fixed numeric references identify them. The highlighted bottom-right r3c3 shows an immutable2. Every other cell has its own integral numeral indicators.
text.rules: Place digits1,2,3 so each appears exactly once in every completed row and column. A mutable blank is0. Place only in a blank cell and clear a filled mutable cell before replacing it. No two filled cells may repeat a digit in a row or column. The fixed2 removes the digit2 choice from r1c3,r2c3,r3c1,r3c2. Other offered digits include recoverable mistakes.
text.clues: Each fixed two-stroke inequality points at its smaller cell: r1c1<r1c2, r2c1<r2c2 and r2c3<r1c3. A clue with a blank endpoint does not compare values yet. When both are filled, strict numeric order must hold. Thus a smaller3 or larger1 can be placed while its neighbor is blank but can create a dead end. No automatic deduction is performed.
text.solution: The unique full square is123/231/312 from far row to near row. The following literal choices are an example solution, not an automatic solver. Clear mutable cells individually to return to eight blanks and the same fixed2.
text.backtrack: The partial103/021/312 is a maximal incomplete dead end: no placement remains. Clear r2c2=2, then place r1c2=2,r2c1=2,r2c2=3 to complete123/231/312. Individual clearing is the recovery action; there is no reset.
text.order_examples: From legal partial020/013/002, placing r1c1=3 violates3<2, placing r2c1=2 violates2<1 and placing r1c3=1 violates3<1. These compare distinct digits without a row or column repeat; each independently violates only its own clue.
text.limits: The mutable fields select fixed connected mounted numeral silhouettes, and the given2 is immutable drawing. This is not physical writing, erasing, loose digit custody or material consumption. No score, turn, solver, completion feedback, reset or timer is claimed.
